text:
Alex Kim: Hey @Maria — getting a denial on my recent allergy testing. EOB says 'service billed as global procedure, not covered'. Provider did skin prick + intradermal, I think they should've billed separate CPTs. Has anyone run into this? Need appeal steps or provider rebill guidance.
Maria Chen: Thanks for flagging, Alex. Can you DM me the insurer name + plan ID and a pic/PDF of the EOB? Usually two paths: 1) provider rebills with discrete CPTs; or 2) file an appeal with the insurer attaching procedure notes.
Alex Kim: DM sent with EOB and claim #. Provider invoice says code 95004 and a lump total.
Susan Alvarez: I can reach out to the clinic. If they rebill we often get faster resolution. Please forward the invoice to provider-relations@redwood.com and cc me.
Maria Chen: For the appeal route, we'll need: insurer appeal form (if any), itemized invoice, procedure note from provider, and a short member statement. I can help assemble.
Jordan (People Ops): Pasting a quick sample appeal text you can copy into the insurer portal. Make sure to attach the procedure note and the itemized bill.
Jordan (People Ops): ```
To: Appeals Department
Member: Alex Kim
Subscriber ID: [insert]
Claim #: [insert]
Date of Service: 2026-11-03
Provider: Evergreen Allergy Clinic

Appeal: The claim for allergy testing was denied with reason 'global procedure not covered.' The services rendered included separate skin prick testing and intradermal testing which should be billed as distinct CPT codes (e.g., 95004 series) and supported by the attached procedure note. We request reconsideration and payment per the member's in-network benefits.

Attachments: itemized invoice; procedure note; EOB
Contact: Alex Kim, alex.k@redwood.com, (555) 555-1212

Sincerely,
Alex Kim
```
Benefits Bot: Thanks — claim 0xA9F4 queued. If you choose to appeal, upload attachments here: https://insurer.example.com/appeals (use claim # 0xA9F4). Typical review time 6-8 weeks; expediting possible if provider rebills.
Alex Kim: Thanks all — I've forwarded invoice to provider-relations and started the insurer appeal with the sample text. Any tips to speed this up? :pray:
Maria Chen: If the provider can rebill with itemized CPTs and a procedure note, escalate to them to rebill electronically (electronic rebill + updated claim often resolves in 2–3 weeks). Otherwise, appeal turnaround is longer. Keep all receipts.
Susan Alvarez: I emailed the clinic contact and asked for a rebill request. If they confirm, I'll let you know here so you can withdraw the appeal if needed. :thumbsup:
Alex Kim: Awesome — appreciate it.
Maria Chen: Keep us posted. If you need a template to request the provider rebill, I can drop one here.
Jordan (People Ops): I'll add a short provider-rebill template to the thread later today.
Benefits Bot: Reminder: appeals with complete attachments have higher overturn rates. Good luck! :sparkles:
